title: Vascular aging and arterial stiffening
bottleneck: Arteries stiffen with age through elastin fragmentation, collagen crosslinking (advanced glycation end-products), and endothelial dysfunction, driving hypertension, heart failure, and stroke. Unlike cholesterol, arterial stiffness has no approved drug therapy; AGE-breakers like alagebrium failed clinically, and the causal chain from stiffness to end-organ damage is still being mapped.
why_it_blocks: Cardiovascular disease kills more older adults than any other cause, and vascular aging underlies it. Without a therapy targeting the vessel wall itself, prevention stays limited to risk-factor control that does not reverse stiffness.
current_state: Management is blood pressure and lipid control plus exercise. Pulse-wave velocity is a research biomarker, not a treatment target in guidelines. Senolytics are being explored for vascular calcification and stiffness. Crosslink breakers failed clinically, shifting attention to senolytics and anti-fibrotic approaches for the vessel wall, though no therapy has yet reduced arterial stiffness in humans.
